date_enacted: 2026-06-04 (Coachella City Council special meeting approved an interim urgency moratorium on data centers, per NBC Palm Springs and kvcrnews.org reporting); extended on or about 2026-07-09 while the city drafts a permanent ban
duration: Consistent with the Gov. Code section 65858 interim urgency ordinance pattern already documented elsewhere in this inventory (initial up to 45 days, extendable to a 2-year maximum by 4/5 vote): reported as an initial temporary/urgency moratorium adopted 2026-06-04, then extended around 2026-07-09 ('Coachella Extends Temporary Ban On Data Center Developments,' Patch) as the council moves toward a permanent ban. Exact day counts and vote margins were not confirmed in the sources reviewed.
legal_basis: Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 1229 (adopted 2026-06-04, 45-day pause); extended by Urgency Ordinance No. 1230 (adopted 2026-07-08/09, 10 months 15 days); superseded by Ordinance No. 1231, adding Chapter 17.92 to the Coachella Municipal Code to permanently prohibit data center uses citywide (first reading 2026-08-12, second reading/adoption 2026-08-26, effective 30 days after adoption).
trigger: Public backlash and protests over a large proposed data center project and a power agreement with developer 'Stronghold'; council terminated the specific project and moved toward a permanent ban
current_status: Replaced as of 2026-09-23. The City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1231 on 2026-08-26 (second reading), permanently prohibiting data center uses citywide (with limited exceptions for accessory server/IT rooms); effective 2026-09-25, thirty days after adoption. Mayor Figueroa has also voiced support for a future ballot measure to entrench the ban, but no such measure had been placed on a ballot as of this pass.
affected_projects: A large proposed data center project tied to a power agreement with 'Stronghold'; project reported terminated by the city (per NBC Palm Springs, 'Coachella City Council Halts Data Center Project, Cuts Ties with Stronghold,' 2026-06-05)
outcome: Moratorium adopted (Ord. 1229) and extended 10 months 15 days (Ord. 1230); superseded by a permanent citywide prohibition on data centers (Ord. 1231), adopted 2026-08-26 and effective 2026-09-25. Coachella is the first Coachella Valley city and second California city (after Monterey Park) to permanently ban data centers.
